evidence.observedFact: The active venue publishes current weekly hours, promotes private parties, online gift cards, league nights, and upcoming private-party closures.

The venue rents the parlor for private events for up to 60 guests, publishes hourly rental pricing, requires typically at least 48 hours advance notice, and offers a message path for questions before booking.
The Cleveland Pinball League uses recurring multi-week participation and the venue also promotes a monthly family-friendly pinball battle, demonstrating repeat-event behavior.

gaps.recommendedFix: Demonstrate an event-to-repeat-visit workflow that captures private-party and tournament guests and gives them a reason to return after the event.
Use recurring league, tournament, and gift-card audiences for permission-based comeback offers between visits and seasons.
Demonstrate automated acknowledgement and follow-up for private-event questions and booking inquiries while preserving the existing booking process.

notes: Observed facts show a strong recurring-event and private-party model. The opportunity is to demonstrate measurable post-event retention and reactivation; public evidence does not prove the business currently lacks an internal retention system or establish any monetary loss.
